issues.legal_issue: The scope of a legislative grant of power to tax income as applied to gains realized from the sale of capital assets.
material_facts: A taxpayer realized a gain from the sale of an interest in immovable property, and the gain was included in the taxpayer’s assessment under a statutory capital-gains provision.
The taxpayer challenged the levy on the ground that the central legislature lacked legislative competence to impose it.
The relevant legislative grant authorized laws concerning taxes on income other than agricultural income.
issues.conclusion: The gain fell within the meaning of income in the legislative grant, so the central legislature had power to impose the tax and the provision was not ultra vires on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Words in a constitutional enactment conferring legislative power are read in their ordinary, natural and grammatical meaning, with a liberal construction giving them their widest reasonable amplitude. The ordinary meaning of income includes a profit or gain actually received, including a capital gain. Judicial interpretations of income in particular income-tax statutes do not establish a restrictive legislative practice that narrows its ordinary meaning in a constitutional legislative entry. The Court applied the broad-construction principles in In re The Central Provinces and Berar Act No. XIV of 1938, The United Provinces v. Atiqa Begum, and State of Bombay v. F. N. Balsara, and relied on the broad conception of income discussed in Kamakshya Narain Singh v. Commissioner of Income-tax and in Eisner v. Macomber, Merchants’ Loan & Trust Co. v. Smietanka, United States v. Stewart, and Resch v. Federal Commissioner of Taxation. It distinguished the context-specific interpretations in Commissioner of Income-tax v. Shaw Wallace & Co., Ryall v. Hoare and Ryall v. Honeywill, Californian Copper Syndicate v. Harris, Wallace Brothers & Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, and Croft v. Dunphy.

predicates.legislative_competence_challenge: The proceeding challenges whether a legislature had authority to enact a tax.
predicates.income_taxing_grant_applies: The applicable constitutional grant gives the legislature power to make laws concerning taxes on income.
predicates.gain_realized_from_asset_sale_is_taxed: The legislature imposes a tax on a gain actually realized from the sale of an asset.
predicates.capital_gains_tax_falls_within_income_ta: A tax on a realized capital gain falls within the legislature’s power to tax income.

issues.definition: When a proceeding challenges legislative authority to tax a gain realized from an asset sale and an applicable grant confers power to tax income, the rule treats the capital-gains tax as within that power.
